liveTrench.guidance: When WebGL2 is available (`site/fx.js`), every raster ridge and the canvas glyph field give way to one live ASCII shader: the ridge is a candle chart (4 cells per candle, body, centre wick, gap) that scrolls one cell every 420ms and prints a new candle every 4 steps from the right, its forming candle ticking every 160ms. Glyphs come from the ramp ` .·:-=+*x#%@█`, picked per cell by brightness; ink #ededed only, alpha .42 desktop and .34 phone, 9 by 16 px cells (7 by 13 on phones). It draws at about 6 fps at rest, since nothing changes faster than the 160ms tick, and at 30 fps only while the pointer or a key-press ring is moving it. The ridge starts 32px above the stage, normalized to the viewport and bounded between 24 percent and the old 57 percent desktop / 62 percent phone positions. Its vertical span stays 27 percent desktop / 20 percent phone. It recalculates when the viewport or hero size changes, keeping the live field visible above the compact demo. The pointer lifts the ridge under it and brightens nearby glyphs; each key the tour presses sends a ring through the field from the HUD. All raster ridges and the separate glyph canvas are hidden while the live renderer runs, so differently scaled glyph grids never overlap. The raster layers are fallback-only. It pauses when the tab is hidden, draws one still frame under reduced motion, and the plates return if the context is lost. A head script marks `<html class="webgl2">` so WebGL2 browsers never download the near plates; `fx.js` removes the mark whenever the live trench cannot run.

cursors.guidance: 1-bit pixel hand at 2x (site/assets/cursors/hand.svg, hotspot 9 1), green on clickable (hand-pop.svg). The SVGs still use #ededed on #0a0a0a. Touch, forced colours and higher-contrast keep the native cursor.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Lit Device"**

The page is the product running. The real CLI, drawn cell for cell by the app itself, plays inside a graphite bezel that is tilted back 7deg like a device on a desk and flattens when you reach for it. Everything else on the page is quiet enough to let it be the brightest thing. Surfaces are near-black tinted green (#080a09 page, #0e1310 cards), text is a soft green-white, and there is exactly one accent: a green (#4ade80) that means live, selected or confirmed.

The page chrome and the terminal screen are now two palettes. The chrome follows the owner's surface-role brief (2026-10-19). The screen still renders the CLI's own `mono` theme frames, which are generated tour data, so the screen content stays black, white and grey with the app's muted up and down. Nothing in `packages/tui/src/theme.ts` changed.

Prose is set in Spline Sans; headlines, labels, commands and anything technical are set in Spline Sans Mono; JetBrains Mono draws only terminal cells and the trench. Controls share one language: a card with an inset 1px border, a segmented switch whose thumb stretches and lands, and a command band with a Copy button. Behind it all runs a full-bleed ASCII trench that steps back past the first screen.
keyCharacteristics: Green-tinted surface roles, one green accent, a white Copy button as the strongest control.
Two leaning devices: the stage and the analyst panel. Cards carry a soft shadow.
One component family reused for the installer (hero and closing section) and the agent hookup: spotlight card, rubber segment, command band, Copy.
Rem-scaled layout (Osmo scaling) so the composition holds its proportions between design frames.
Four named easings plus `--ease-out` on the stage; reduced motion removes all animation.

rules.name: The Two Palettes Rule
rules.body: Page chrome uses the tokens above. The terminal screen renders the CLI's `mono` theme frames (generated by `packages/cli/tools/site-frames.mjs`), so its colours come from the app, not from this file. Do not recolour screen content to match the page, and do not hand-edit frames. Terminal glyphs whose colour is under 1.4:1 contrast on their background (the app's decrypt fade) render as empty cells on the page.

rules.name: The One Green Rule
rules.body: Green means live, selected or confirmed. No second accent, no gradient fills with hue beyond the soft green under-glow of the devices.

rules.name: The Strongest Control Rule
rules.body: The Copy button (ink fill, page text) and the Install button are the only solid light fills. It turns green and reads "Copied" on success.

rules.name: The Machine Voice Rule
rules.body: Mono is for headlines, labels, commands, keys and source names. Sentences are Spline Sans.

rules.name: The Tight Display Rule
rules.body: Letter-spacing tightens as size grows (-0.035em at title, -0.04em at display, -0.045em at headline); body stays at 1.6 to 1.75.

rules.name: The Soft Card Rule
rules.body: A card is the page's content surface: card fill, inset border, soft shadow. Do not stack a card inside a card; the command band runs full bleed with hairlines instead.

rules.name: The Two Leaning Devices Rule
rules.body: Only the stage and the analyst panel lean. Any third leaning object needs a new owner decision.

dos: **Do** take page colours from the frontmatter tokens and keep green to live, selected and confirmed states.
**Do** build new controls from the installer parts: card, rubber segment, command band, Copy.
**Do** use Spline Sans for sentences and Spline Sans Mono for headlines, labels and commands.
**Do** use rem for layout so the Osmo scaling holds; render desktop and the 390px frame.
**Do** keep controls at least 2.75rem tall on touch and keep a visible focus ring.
**Do** regenerate the tour with `site-frames.mjs` whenever the app's look changes.
**Do** put provenance (a `.webp.json` sidecar) beside every shipping raster.
donts: **Don't** use em dashes (U+2014) anywhere in copy, code comments or docs.
**Don't** put arrows or chevrons on buttons or calls to action.
**Don't** hand-draw, recolour or screenshot-edit the CLI screen; frames come from the app.
**Don't** present the npm or Homebrew names as live until they are published.
**Don't** replace the events row with a scrolling ticker.
**Don't** nest a card in a card, or lean a third object.
